entries.headline: Borderlands 4 joins Xbox Free Play Days with different access rules across the lineup
entries.summary: Xbox announced its September 10–13 Free Play Days lineup. Borderlands 4, F1 25 2026 Edition, Surviving Mars: Relaunched and CarX Drift Racing Online are available to Game Pass Ultimate, Premium and Essential members. Dustborn offers a two-hour trial. EA Sports Madden NFL 27 is available to all Xbox players without those Game Pass memberships; access conditions and trial limits differ by title.

entries.headline: Gears of War marks the fifth year of its Never Fight Alone campaign
entries.summary: Gears of War announced the fifth year of Never Fight Alone, its suicide-prevention partnership with Crisis Text Line. The Coalition donates 1% of net product revenue, and the initiative has supported more than 16,000 crisis-support conversations. A charity bundle arriving with Gears of War: E-Day on October 6 will donate all its net revenue to Crisis Text Line.

entries.headline: CONTROL Resonant expands Assist Mode with individual combat adjustments
entries.summary: Remedy detailed CONTROL Resonant’s Assist Mode, with separate controls for enemy aggression, the Perfect Dodge Window, projectile speed, damage and power recovery. Options also include immortality and one-hit kills. Players can toggle the mode during play, lower the challenge or make combat harder by increasing enemy aggression and tightening the dodge window. The game is scheduled to launch on September 24.

entries.headline: BrokenLore: DON’T LIE launches as its developer discusses horror and social themes
entries.summary: Serafini Productions founder Sebastiano Serafini announced BrokenLore: DON’T LIE’s release on Xbox Wire and outlined its narrative themes. Junko, a socially withdrawn young woman, confronts past trauma as memory and reality begin to blur. The developer describes it as both a standalone story and part of the series’ connected exploration of social issues through horror.

entries.headline: Professor Layton and the Curious Village Remake announced for multiple platforms in 2027
entries.summary: IGN and Gematsu report that LEVEL-5 announced Professor Layton and the Curious Village Remake for PS5, Switch 2, Switch and PC via Steam in 2027. The remake reimagines the original game’s characters in 3D and adds richer environmental detail. IGN also reports higher-resolution, widescreen animated cutscenes. A specific release date has not been announced.
